origin.description: Extract the first segment between text boundaries.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: opts_brkiter
arguments.text: Break-iterator settings. NULL uses the line breaker.
Further settings passed to stri_opts_brkiter, including type, locale, and skip_*.

origin.details: Vectorized over str. A skip_* flag drops every segment whose ending boundary has that ICU rule status. The skipped text is not joined to the next segment. An omitted skip acts as FALSE. Indexes are 1-based inclusive code points. No segment, an empty string, or a missing string is NA.
origin.value: A character vector. NA marks no segment.
origin.example:
x <- stri_extract_first_boundaries("ab cd", type = "character")
cat(paste0('stri_extract_first_boundaries("ab cd", type = "character") returns ', x, '.\n'))

translation.description: Extract the first segment between text boundaries.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: opts_brkiter
arguments.text: A dict of supplied break-iterator settings. None uses the line breaker.

arguments.name: kwargs
arguments.text: Further settings passed to stri_opts_brkiter. A repeated name is an error.

translation.details: A skip_* flag drops every segment whose ending boundary has that ICU rule status. The skipped text is not joined to the next segment. An omitted skip is false. Positions are 1-based inclusive code points. BreakIterator indexes are UTF-16 code units and are converted before they are returned. NA stays missing. The string "NA" is text. No segment, an empty string, or a missing string is NA.
translation.value: A list of strings. NA marks no segment.
translation.example:
from stringi.boundary import stri_extract_first_boundaries
x = stri_extract_first_boundaries("ab cd", type="character")
print(f'stri_extract_first_boundaries("ab cd", type="character") returns {x[0]}.')
